threads.body: Every scenario in this package omits `metrics`, so the runner skips metric checks entirely (`tools/runner/src/opentelemetry/conformance/_spec.py:141-144` and `_checks.py:104-112`). Because the committed coverage records `db.client.operation.duration`, a regression that removes that Cassandra metric would still pass. Add `metrics: [db.client.operation.duration]` to each scenario, as the existing Java database packages do.

threads.body: This pin is meant to retain the driver 4.0–4.3 instrumentation path, but the Gradle update rule in `.github/renovate.json5:45–49` allows minor upgrades and there is no Cassandra-specific version bound. A normal Renovate update to 4.4+ would silently turn this package into another run of the newer instrumentation line, losing the early-driver coverage. Add a file/package-scoped Renovate rule restricting `com.datastax.oss:java-driver-core` to versions below 4.4.

replies.body:
Addressed in a0a82a77ee792e3cd46336c9a1ec34dcaa5a052b.

The frozen catalog assigns com.datastax.oss:java-driver-core version 4.3.1 to the early-driver launcher, and scenarios/database/README.md:7-9 explicitly preserves distinct 4.0-4.3 and 4.4+ instrumentation coverage. The new file/package-scoped Renovate rule caps only that coordinate in the database catalog at <4.4. Native Renovate matching and Maven release filtering confirm 4.3 patch updates remain allowed, 4.4+ is rejected, and Apache driver updates and other catalogs are unchanged.

`{present: true}` lets any error pass. The Redis contracts pin the value, and Cassandra semconv makes `db.response.status_code` conditionally required on failure (Invalid = `0x2200`), which `data.json` shows is not emitted today. Worth pinning both so the gap shows up:

```suggestion
            error.type: com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.servererrors.InvalidQueryException
            db.response.status_code: "8704"
```

threads.body:
The session has no keyspace, so `db.namespace` (conditionally required, the session keyspace for Cassandra) is never exercised. SQL contracts assert `db.namespace: conformance`; binding the keyspace here would let the contract do the same:

```suggestion
            .withLocalDatacenter(ScenarioEnvironment.require("CASSANDRA_LOCAL_DATACENTER"))
            .withKeyspace("conformance")
```

These re-assert the package YAML and pin the exact set of Cassandra packages (same for the exact `:shared:cassandra*` set in `test_java_project_discovery.py`). No other backend has tests like this, and adding any new Cassandra package or client will break them. CI already runs the packages, so I'd drop them.
